name: AG2
description: AG2 (formerly AutoGen): The Open-Source AgentOS.Join us at: https://discord.gg/sNGSwQME3x
editorialSummary: AG2 is the community-led continuation of the original AutoGen multi-agent framework (AgentOS), with active development around conversable agents, group chat, and tool use.
whyCare: If you want AutoGen-style multi-agent conversations with an actively maintained open fork, AG2 is the primary upstream to track.
notes: Community fork/continuation of AutoGen; prefer this over microsoft/autogen for new OSS AutoGen-lineage work.

name: Agno
description: Build, run, and manage agent platforms.
editorialSummary: Agno (formerly Phidata) is a high-performance Python framework for building agents and multi-agent systems with built-in tooling for memory, knowledge, and agent platform runtime concerns.
whyCare: Strong ergonomics and performance for shipping agent apps and platforms without bolting on half a dozen libs.

name: CAMEL
description: 🐫 CAMEL: The first and the best multi-agent framework. Finding the Scaling Law of Agents. https://www.camel-ai.org
editorialSummary: CAMEL is a research-rooted multi-agent framework exploring communicative agents and scaling laws of agent societies. It offers role-playing societies, tool agents, and extensive research tooling.
whyCare: Strong research pedigree for multi-agent communication experiments and agent-society simulations beyond simple task crews.

name: CrewAI
description: Framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous AI agents. By fostering collaborative intelligence, CrewAI empowers agents to work together seamlessly, tackling complex tasks.
editorialSummary: CrewAI focuses on role-based multi-agent crews and process flows that are approachable for product teams. Agents collaborate with defined roles, tools, and tasks without requiring a heavy graph model.
whyCare: Fast path from idea to a working multi-agent team—strong DX for role-playing crews and sequential/hierarchical processes.

name: Google Agent Development Kit
description: An open-source, code-first Python toolkit for building, evaluating, and deploying sophisticated AI agents with flexibility and control.
editorialSummary: Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK) is a code-first toolkit for building, evaluating, and deploying multi-agent systems with strong Google Cloud / Gemini alignment.
whyCare: Official Google path for sophisticated multi-agent apps with eval and deployment hooks—especially if you are already on Gemini/GCP.

name: smolagents
description: 🤗 smolagents: a barebones library for agents that think in code.
editorialSummary: Hugging Face smolagents is a minimal library for code-acting agents that write and run code to solve tasks. Designed to be readable and hackable rather than a full enterprise platform.
whyCare: Lightweight entry point for code-first agents with tight HF Hub integration and clear educational value.

name: LangGraph
editorialSummary: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework for durable, stateful agent workflows as graphs of nodes and edges. It emphasizes checkpointing, human-in-the-loop, and production reliability on top of the LangChain ecosystem.
whyCare: Best-in-class control for complex agent loops—cycles, branching, persistence, and streaming—when you outgrow simple chain/agent wrappers.

name: Dify
description: Build Agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, with rich AI model and tool support on one collaborative workspace. Deploy on cloud, VPC, or self-hosted, so teams move from prototype to production without rebuilding the stack.
editorialSummary: Dify is a self-hostable agentic workflow and RAG platform with a visual builder, tool integrations, and team workspace features. It sits between low-code product tooling and developer frameworks.
whyCare: Ship agentic apps with a UI + backend stack you can self-host—ideal when non-engineers need to design agent workflows.
notes: License is a modified Apache-2.0 with additional commercial/multi-tenant restrictions (GitHub SPDX NOASSERTION); not plain Apache-2.0.

name: AutoGen
description: A programming framework for agentic AI
editorialSummary: Microsoft’s AutoGen popularized conversable multi-agent patterns and remains an important reference implementation. Maintenance has slowed relative to the AG2 community fork; check both before committing.
whyCare: Historically shaped multi-agent chat and tool-calling patterns; still useful as ecosystem reference and enterprise Microsoft alignment.
notes: Code under LICENSE-CODE (MIT); repo root LICENSE is CC-BY-4.0 for docs. Community continuation: ag2ai/ag2. Last notable push ~Apr 2026.

name: Semantic Kernel
description: Integrate cutting-edge LLM technology quickly and easily into your apps
editorialSummary: Semantic Kernel is Microsoft’s SDK for embedding planners, plugins, and agentic patterns into .NET, Python, and Java apps. Strong fit for enterprise stacks already on Azure/.NET.
whyCare: Enterprise-friendly agent and plugin model with first-class .NET support—rare among Python-heavy agent frameworks.

name: OpenAI Agents SDK
description: A lightweight, powerful framework for multi-agent workflows
editorialSummary: OpenAI’s production-oriented Agents SDK for multi-agent handoffs, tools, and tracing. It succeeds the educational Swarm patterns with a clearer programming model and first-party observability.
whyCare: Canonical OpenAI stack for agent handoffs and tool use, with lightweight APIs suitable for production multi-agent apps.
notes: Spiritual successor to openai/swarm educational patterns.

name: Swarm
description: Educational framework exploring ergonomic, lightweight multi-agent orchestration. Managed by OpenAI Solution team.
editorialSummary: Swarm is OpenAI’s educational exploration of lightweight multi-agent handoffs and routines. It is not a production SDK; patterns live on in the OpenAI Agents SDK.
whyCare: Short, readable reference for handoff-style multi-agent design—historically useful, then move to openai-agents-python for real apps.
notes: Educational only; OpenAI points production users to openai/openai-agents-python. No GitHub Releases; last push ~Apr 2026.

name: Pydantic AI
description: AI Agent Framework, the Pydantic way
editorialSummary: Pydantic AI brings type-safe, dependency-injected agent definitions using Pydantic models for structured outputs and tooling. Strong fit for teams that already standardize on Pydantic/FastAPI.
whyCare: Typed agent interfaces and structured outputs with familiar Pydantic ergonomics—great for production Python services.

name: AutoGPT
description: AutoGPT is the vision of accessible AI for everyone, to use and to build on. Our mission is to provide the tools, so that you can focus on what matters.
editorialSummary: AutoGPT ignited the 2023 autonomous-agent wave and remains a landmark project. The monorepo now mixes the classic agent with a newer platform under a different license—treat as historically essential, not the default modern framework pick.
whyCare: Historically significant autonomous-agent milestone; useful for studying early agent loops and the evolving AutoGPT platform.
notes: Split licensing: autogpt_platform/ is Polyform Shield; classic agent and other paths are MIT. Still actively pushed, but prefer LangGraph/CrewAI/Agents SDK for greenfield production agents.
